clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Gordon dying in June 1991, within three years: your wrist injury stopped your playing and you lost your footing in October 1991, then you and Rafe had a blow-up and he moved out that November. You were on your own getting high and absorbed in fixing radios by late 1991, then lost and low by January 1992 with your grandfather gone and your mother about to remarry. Your anxiety climbed and your functioning fell. By the time you were at community college in autumn 1992, a bleak year of nights out playing pool and days asleep, your symptom was up and your functioning down. Alongside these months, your stepfather Desmond settled with your mother and you at the rebuilt Hollin Road house in September 1989, you began at the conservatory in September 1991, and your sister Tara was born in July 1990. Your grandmother Winifred was treated for a thyroid tumour within a year or so of being widowed around the same time. By January 1994 you were stung that your dad had never heard of the film you were making, and you found your drive again with an exchange in Lisbon and Porto later that month; things improved. Your cousin Bella was treated for melanoma in 1994 alongside these shifts, held as a reaction in the wider family.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's death, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Winifred found to have bowel cancer in 2001 or 2002, within three years: you were running out of steam for performing by September 2001, your anxiety climbed and your functioning fell. You had a disastrous audition for the national orchestra in early 2002 and were done with performing. You were on poor terms with family and friends and left Thornbury for Gull Harbour in September 2002. You met Marisol at a winter party in January 2003 and moved to Fenwick with her in June 2003, then split up within the year by October 2003. Once you were back in Thornbury that November, you sank into a deep depression, your symptom was up and your functioning down. You could not face your family and your anxiety climbed; your parents seemed a world away. You relied, gingerly, on friends. Your father spoke with Corbin, who took you in. You began swimming laps and requested help from your parents with therapy costs in January 2004. You returned to your therapist Victor Halloran that January and your functioning rose. Your grandmother spent her final months in a back bedroom of Maureen and Desmond's home in September 2003, then died of the bowel cancer in February 2004. Your last visit to her sickroom was brief and hung over, on the way to the airport in January 2004; you cut it short and regret it. The period settles where you turned to a helper and your functioning began to rise.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008–2009

You stopped speaking to your mother when you moved to Marlow Sound for nursing school in August 2008 and began the nursing programme in September 2008; the silence held for roughly a year. The period is of your cutoff from your mother and your aunt's illness in the same months, neither clearly settled by the end of the year.
